A1.justification: The authors, SAOR/UGDA procedures, source datasets and 95,839-image corpus establish continuity despite the DiQuID-to-SAGI-D rename. Both PDFs are readable throughout, including v2's supplementary Sections 6–9. v1 mentions supplementary details but ends with references; judgments concern material actually included in the supplied PDFs.

before.justification: v1 reports original detector evaluations, compression experiments, prompt ablations and a 42-participant human study in Section 4.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds caption-prompt comparisons, cross-dataset evaluations and supplementary quantitative and qualitative analyses.

M1.justification: SAOR retains caption/object-conditioned LLM prompting, and UGDA retains its initial realism check, reversed-order comparisons and formal classification rule. MMII's operations remain in the dataset-generation description despite losing their separate component heading. The SAGI name and expanded implementation explanations do not establish a new algorithm.

E1.justification: TGIF, previously used for dataset-quality comparisons, becomes training and testing data for forensic detection/localization in v2 Table 5. This extends coverage within the existing inpainting domain. The COCO/RAISE/OpenImages corpus, manipulation types and principal human-study population remain.

E2.justification: v2 adds object-label-plus-caption prompting as a SAOR comparator and directly compares UGDA with AS, QAlign and CLIP quality/aesthetic measures for separating human-perceived realism (Tables 1–2). Table 5 adds TGIF-trained detector variants as controls. The underlying four forensic architectures remain PSCC, CAT-Net, MMFusion and TruFor.

E3.justification: v2 introduces cross-dataset training/testing, detection and localization AUC, test-set adjustments described as preventing leakage, CLIP quality scoring, and metric-ranked top/bottom halves for realism evaluation. It also changes the stated generation setting from two additional inpainting rounds to one on one-sixth of images; regeneration is not established. The original corpus splits and compression settings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 expands prompt ablation with a caption control and per-pipeline results, tests UGDA against quality/aesthetic rankings, and adds single-versus-double manipulation, pipeline-specific, demographic and human SP/FR analyses. Supplementary figures examine localization errors and generation failure modes. The compression analysis is retained in Section 8.2, while the numerical prompt-fidelity comparison is dropped.

E5.justification: v2 Section 8.3 adds chi-square independence tests, p-values and Cramer's V for demographic associations, using 34 participants after filtering. Both versions retain 3–5 human assessments per image; neither reports detector seed variability or confidence intervals. The new statistical procedure is confined to this supplementary analysis.

E6.justification: v2 adds cross-dataset AUC and numerous subgroup and qualitative results. Retained reports also change: object/LLM QAlign quality averages move from 4.16/4.17 in v1 Table 3 to 3.96/3.96 in v2 Table 1. Retrained TruFor's 'All' accuracy/IoU changes from 0.95/0.68 to 99.7/87.6 in v2 Table 13, without a clear setting explanation and with conflicting accompanying prose. These are revised reports, not established same-setting gains. Some fidelity entries are removed.

T1.justification: v2 Equations 1–2 introduce a limited probabilistic formalization: image semantics are approximated by captions and object lists, and a human-conditioned prompt/object distribution is approximated by an LLM. This adds explicit mathematical assumptions to v1's procedural description. No theorem, proof or theoretical guarantee is added; the UGDA decision rule remains equivalent.

C1.justification: The central contribution shifts from a large forensic benchmark and its construction methodology to SAGI as a general framework for automated realistic generation and test-time assessment, with SAGI-D as an application. The abstract and contributions recast the existing 74%-versus-35% human group difference as a drop after applying the framework. The largest-dataset and detector-training utility claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 interprets order sensitivity as aleatoric uncertainty relative to a learned semantic distribution and argues that quality/aesthetic scores inadequately measure realism. Supplementary discussion adds specific explanations involving CAT-Net's JPEG assumptions, PSCC underfitting, out-of-mask changes and prompt/generation failures. It also introduces demographic interpretations, although the claimed non-rejection of independence conflicts with Table 12's small p-values at conventional significance levels.

D1.justification: v2 Sections 6.3–6.7 supply previously unavailable system prompts, API identifiers and dates, temperatures, top-p values, token limits, prompt processing, pipeline/model configurations and human-interface details. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation without establishing implementation changes. The code/data access pointer changes from DiQuID to SAGI. Conversely, v1's explicit validation-based checkpoint-selection statement is omitted.

R1.justification: v2 adds an image quality/aesthetic assessment subsection covering NIMA, HyperIQA, MUSIQ, VILA and related methods, positioning realism assessment as a distinct gap. It introduces literature on human prompting and image realism while substantially condensing the earlier detection survey, including removal of its SPAN, CFL-Net and FOCAL discussions. This changes research positioning beyond bibliographic editing.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contribution list, methodological narrative and conclusion are extensively rewritten around SAGI. Experiments are reordered to foreground image quality and realism before forensic benchmarking. Dataset splits, compression analysis and human/model comparison material move into the supplement, alongside expanded explanations and new subsections.

P2.justification: v2 redraws and combines the two pipeline diagrams into Figure 1, restructures the prompting and dataset-comparison tables, and adds prompt panels, analysis tables, localization maps and success/failure galleries. The original example montage is retained as Figure 2, the compression plot moves unchanged to Figure 6, and the split table moves to Table 6.

improvement.justification: The caption control, TGIF transfer experiments and explicit prompts/settings address validation and reproducibility gaps in v1, providing a limited net improvement. However, new reporting problems weaken parts of the expanded evidence: Tables 2 and 13 give conflicting human IoU patterns, the Table 5 discussion misattributes numerical gains, and Section 8.3's non-rejection claim conflicts with Table 12's p-values. These problems limit the overall benefit despite the substantial additions.
